ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a large triangular grid composed of many congruent small equilateral triangles. The left and right boundaries of the gray shaded part are both vertical line segments, the bottom side lies on the horizontal grid line at the bottom of the large triangle, and the top side is a line segment slanting from the upper left to the upper right. Therefore the outer contour of the shaded region can be regarded as a trapezoid whose parallel sides are the left and right vertical sides. Counting by the grid, the left vertical side of the shaded region spans upward from the bottom side across the heights of 4 small triangles, and the right vertical side of the shaded region spans upward from the bottom side across the heights of 5 small triangles; the horizontal distance between the two vertical sides is 2.5 small-triangle side lengths. Reasoning: Let the side length of each small equilateral triangle be s, and its height be h. The problem gives that the area of each small triangle is 1, so sh/2=1, that is, sh=2. The two parallel side lengths of the shaded trapezoid are 4h and 5h respectively, and the distance between them is 2.5s. The area of the trapezoid is ((4h+5h)/2)×(2.5s)=11.25sh. Substituting sh=2 gives the area 11.25×2=22.5.
